answer: Anchor each identity to one registered saffron plot beside a vineyard at a desert oasis: the plot's soil sensor signs a fresh moisture-and-temperature curve each epoch, cross-checked against satellite NDVI for that parcel. One plot, one vote; two identities sharing a sensor report the same curve and collapse to one, burning their bond. A farm wanting one hundred votes must lease one hundred real plots at about $240 per year each, buy one hundred sensors at $60, and tend each field for a season. No vote without a fresh signed curve, and the cost of the next identity equals the last.
